headline: AI capex jitters and Intel's guidance miss spark a risk-off slide
body: Friday's session was the clearest risk-off signal of the week: the Nasdaq Composite fell roughly 2.9%, its worst day since June, as Intel sank more than 25% on a disappointing third-quarter forecast and dragged the Philadelphia semiconductor index down over 7%. The S&P 500 and Dow followed tech lower, closing out a month in which the Nasdaq lost more than 5%, its roughest October since last spring. Within the Magnificent Seven, the damage was uneven rather than broad-based: Alphabet suffered its worst post-earnings reaction on record earlier in the week, while Tesla stood out as the lone gainer. That divergence suggests investors are pricing company-specific execution risk around AI spending plans rather than retreating from risk assets wholesale.

The macro backdrop added to the unease rather than offsetting it. The Fed's late-October decision landed as a hold, but policymakers nudged their year-end inflation outlook higher and left the door open to a rate move before year-end, keeping long-end Treasury yields elevated near 5%. Layered on top, the market is still digesting hyperscaler capital-spending guidance from earlier in the month that investors read as aggressive, which has left chip and AI-infrastructure names unusually sensitive to any hint of a demand or margin disappointment. Retail-sentiment chatter on the usual trackers was thin and inconclusive today, so this read leans more on price action and earnings-driven news than on any clear social-media signal heading into next week.
